response.query: What operational drift-detection metrics, window sizes, statistical tests, alert thresholds, and retraining/rollback criteria should be put into post-deployment monitoring for risk-tiered LLMs?
response.answer: For post-deployment monitoring of risk-tiered LLMs, use drift-detection metrics like KL divergence, set window sizes of 1-7 days, apply statistical tests like Kolmogorov-Smirnov, set alert thresholds at 5% drift, and use retraining/rollback criteria when drift exceeds 10%.

results.title: Memory in Large Language Models: Mechanisms, Evaluation and ...
results.content: On this basis, we propose a four-way taxonomy (parametric, contextual, external, and procedural/episodic) and a "memory quadruple" (storage location—persistence—write/access path—controllability), and connect mechanism, evaluation, and governance through a causal chain of "write—read—inhibit/update." To avoid distorted comparisons arising from heterogeneous settings, we provide a three-setting parallel protocol (parameter-only, offline retrieval, online retrieval) that decouples model capability from information availability on the same data slice and timeline; we then construct a layered evaluation: parametric memory (closed-book recall, edit differential, memorization/privacy risks), contextual memory (position–performance curves and the "mid-sequence drop"), external memory (decoupling correctness from snippet-level attribution/faithfulness), and procedural/episodic memory (cross-session consistency and timeline replay, E-MARS+). In evaluation methodology, we provide layered metric systems and reproducible protocols covering the four memory types: for parametric memory, we emphasize factual recall under the PO setting, pre/post-edit differentials, and memorization/privacy risks; for contextual memory, we foreground the diagnosis that "visible ≠\neq usable," with primary reporting via position–performance curves and mid-span drop; for external memory, we decouple retrieval quality from faithfulness/source attribution and jointly report correctness and passage-level groundedness; for procedural/episodic memory, we adopt componentized evaluation of cross-session consistency, timeline replay, and mis-replay control.

results.title: How to Detect and Prevent AI Bias Before Damage Occurs | Galileo
results.content: Discover proven techniques for detecting model bias, measuring AI fairness, and implementing bias mitigation. * **Historical Bias:** Occurs when training data reflects past societal inequities and discrimination, causing models to perpetuate unfair patterns from historical decisions. * **Representation Bias:** Arises when certain demographic groups are underrepresented or inadequately represented in training datasets, leading to poor model performance for those groups. * **Algorithmic Bias:** Results from the model's learning process or optimization objectives that inadvertently favor certain groups over others during training. Together, automated pre-production scans, real-time monitoring, thorough statistical analysis, and adversarial testing create layered protection that keeps unfairness from slipping through, even as your models, data, and users evolve. A straightforward approach trains separate models optimized for different fairness goals—one for demographic parity, another for equalized odds—then combines their scores through weighted voting. * **CI/CD Pipeline Integration for Bias Prevention:** With Galileo, teams can integrate automated metrics directly into their CI/CD pipelines to continuously monitor model performance, facilitating rapid iteration while maintaining bias detection throughout the development lifecycle.
